author: reek
body: This is the direction the compression post-mortem says to write first: their bytes, our reader. Codex cannot sign with this curve and does not want to, so there is no paired signer to agree with and no way for this test to pass by two halves sharing an assumption.

author: reek
body: Every altered byte below is produced by flipping a bit of the original rather than by writing a literal. A control that quietly tests nothing is worse than no control here, because these are the lines that would report a forgery as genuine, and the RSA test next door has already been bitten once by a "different" value that happened to equal the original.

author: reek
body: One bit of s. The signature is still the right width and still a scalar in range, so only the arithmetic can reject it.

author: reek
body: One bit of r. This exercises a different half of the check: r feeds the second scalar multiplication AND is the value the recovered x is compared against, so a wrong r is wrong twice over.

author: reek
body: The genuine signature against a different message.

author: reek
body: s of zero, refused on range before any arithmetic. SEC1 requires the range check and it is not decoration: a zero scalar sails through the inversion and the comparison below can be made to hold.

author: reek
body: A public key one bit off the curve.

author: reek
body: THIS LINE DOES NOT EXERCISE THE CURVE CHECK, and saying so is the point of writing it down. Run with `ec-on-curve` forced to True the output of this whole test is byte-identical: a tampered key fails the arithmetic anyway, so the end-to-end case cannot tell a guard that holds from a guard that does nothing. The same is true of the zero-scalar case above, which yields the point at infinity and is refused there whether or not the range check runs.

author: reek
body: So the two guards are asserted directly, below, where they can fail. The end-to-end lines stay because they pin the answer; they are simply not evidence about these two predicates.

author: reek
body: The range check, both directions. A genuine s is in [1, n-1]; zero is not, and neither is n itself, which is the boundary the comparison has to get right and the one an off-by-one would let through.

author: reek
body: A signature of the wrong width, refused before anything else runs.
